title_en: Law of the People's Republic of China on Prevention of Juvenile Delinquency

articles.content_en: Article 1 This Law is enacted for the purposes of safeguarding the physical and mental health of minors, cultivating their good conduct, and effectively preventing minors from committing illegal and criminal acts.

Article 2 The prevention of juvenile delinquency shall be based on the combination of education and protection of minors, adhere to the principles of prevention first and early intervention, and carry out graded prevention, intervention and correction in a timely manner against the不良 conduct and serious不良 conduct of minors.

Article 3 In carrying out the work of preventing juvenile delinquency, the personal dignity of minors shall be respected, and the legitimate rights and interests of minors such as the right to reputation, the right to privacy, and personal information shall be protected.

Article 4 The prevention of juvenile delinquency shall be carried out through comprehensive governance under the organization of the people's governments at all levels.
State organs, people's organizations, social organizations, enterprises and institutions, residents' committees, villagers' committees, schools, families, and other entities shall each assume their respective responsibilities and cooperate with each other to jointly carry out the work of preventing juvenile delinquency, promptly eliminate all negative factors that breed illegal and criminal acts of minors, and create a favorable social environment for the healthy physical and mental development of minors.

Article 6 The State shall strengthen the construction of specialized schools and provide specialized education for minors with serious不良 conduct. Specialized education is an integral part of the national education system and an important protective disposal measure for educating and correcting minors with serious不良 conduct.
The people's governments of provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government shall incorporate the development of specialized education and the construction of specialized schools into their economic and social development plans. The local people's governments at or above the county level shall establish specialized education steering committees and, as needed, reasonably set up specialized schools.
The specialized education steering committee shall be composed of units such as education, civil affairs, finance, human resources and social security, public security, judicial administration, the People's Procuratorate, the People's Court, the Communist Youth League, the Women's Federation, the Working Committee on Caring for the Next Generation, specialized schools, as well as personnel including lawyers and social workers, to study and determine matters related to the teaching and management of specialized schools.
The specific measures for the construction of specialized schools and specialized education shall be prescribed by the State Council.

Article 7 The public security organs, the People's Procuratorates, the People's Courts, and the judicial administrative departments shall designate specialized organs or specially trained personnel who are familiar with the physical and mental characteristics of minors to be responsible for the work of preventing juvenile delinquency.

Article 8 The Communist Youth League, the Women's Federation, the trade unions, the Disabled Persons' Federation, the Working Committee on Caring for the Next Generation, the Youth Federation, the Students' Federation, the Young Pioneers, and relevant social organizations shall assist the people's governments at all levels and their relevant departments, the People's Procuratorates, and the People's Courts in properly carrying out the work of preventing juvenile delinquency, cultivating social forces for the prevention of juvenile delinquency, and providing support services.

Article 9 The State shall encourage, support, and guide social organizations such as social work service institutions to participate in relevant work concerning the prevention of juvenile delinquency, and shall strengthen supervision.
Article 10 No organization or individual may instigate, coerce, or entice a minor to commit不良 conduct or serious不良 conduct, or provide conditions for a minor to commit the aforesaid acts.

Article 11 Minors shall abide by laws, regulations, and norms of public morality, foster a sense of self-respect, self-discipline, and self-improvement, enhance their ability to distinguish right from wrong and to protect themselves, and consciously resist the inducement and infringement of various不良 conducts and illegal and criminal acts.

Article 12 In preventing juvenile delinquency, the physiological and psychological characteristics of minors at different ages shall be taken into account, and research on adolescent education, psychological care, psychological correction, and crime prevention countermeasures shall be strengthened.

Article 13 The State shall encourage and support the development of disciplines, the establishment of specialties, the cultivation of talents, and scientific research related to the prevention of juvenile delinquency, and shall carry out international exchanges and cooperation.
Article 14 The State shall give commendations and rewards to organizations and individuals that have achieved outstanding results in the work of preventing juvenile delinquency.

Article 15 The State, society, schools, and families shall strengthen education on the core socialist values for minors, carry out crime prevention education, enhance minors' awareness of the rule of law, enable minors to develop the awareness of abiding by laws and disciplines and preventing illegal and criminal acts, and improve their self-control capability.

Article 16 The parents or other guardians of minors shall bear direct responsibility for the crime prevention education of minors, shall perform guardianship duties according to law, establish a good family tradition, and cultivate good conduct in minors; where they discover any abnormality in the psychology or behavior of a minor, they shall promptly understand the situation and carry out education, guidance, and admonition, and shall not refuse or be negligent in performing guardianship duties.

Article 17 The education administrative departments and schools shall incorporate crime prevention education into the school teaching plan, and guide the teaching and administrative staff to, in light of the characteristics of minors, adopt various methods to conduct targeted crime prevention education for minor students.

Article 18 Schools shall employ full-time or part-time teachers engaged in rule-of-law education, and may engage vice-principals for rule-of-law and off-campus rule-of-law counselors from units such as judicial and law enforcement organs, legal education and legal service institutions.

Article 19 Schools shall be equipped with full-time or part-time teachers for mental health education and carry out mental health education. Schools may, based on actual circumstances, cooperate with professional mental health institutions to establish a mental health screening and early intervention mechanism to prevent and address students' psychological and behavioral abnormalities.
Schools shall strengthen communication with the parents or other guardians of minor students, and jointly carry out mental health education for minor students; where it is discovered that a minor student may have a mental disorder, the school shall immediately inform the parents or other guardians to send the student to a relevant professional institution for diagnosis and treatment.

Article 20 The education administrative departments shall, together with relevant departments, establish a system for the prevention and control of student bullying. Schools shall strengthen daily safety management, improve the work procedures for detecting and handling student bullying, strictly investigate and promptly eliminate various potential hazards that may lead to student bullying.

Article 21 The education administrative departments shall encourage and support schools to engage social workers to be stationed in schools on a long-term or regular basis, to assist in carrying out moral education, rule-of-law education, life education, and mental health education, and to participate in the prevention and handling of student bullying and other acts.

Article 22 The education administrative departments and schools shall, through holding lectures, seminars, training and other activities, introduce scientific and reasonable educational methods, and guide the teaching and administrative staff and the parents or other guardians of minor students to effectively prevent juvenile delinquency.
Schools shall inform the parents or other guardians of minor students of the crime prevention education plan. The parents or other guardians of minor students shall cooperate with the schools in conducting targeted crime prevention education for minor students.
Article 23 The education administrative departments shall incorporate the effectiveness of crime prevention education into the annual assessment of schools.

Article 24 The people's governments at all levels and their relevant departments, the People's Procuratorates, the People's Courts, the Communist Youth League, the Young Pioneers, the Women's Federation, the Disabled Persons' Federation, the Working Committee on Caring for the Next Generation, and other entities shall, based on actual circumstances, organize and hold various forms of publicity and education activities on the prevention of juvenile delinquency. Where conditions permit, juvenile rule-of-law education bases may be established to carry out rule-of-law education for minors.

Article 25 The residents' committees and villagers' committees shall actively carry out targeted publicity activities on the prevention of juvenile delinquency, assist the public security organs in maintaining public security around schools, promptly keep abreast of the guardianship, schooling, and employment status of minors within their respective jurisdictions, and organize and guide community social organizations to participate in the work of preventing juvenile delinquency.

Article 26 Off-campus activity venues such as youth palaces and children's activity centers shall take crime prevention education as an important work content and carry out various forms of publicity and education activities.

Article 27 When providing vocational training to minors who have reached the age of sixteen and are preparing for employment, vocational training institutions and employing units shall incorporate crime prevention education into the training content.
Article 29 Where the parents or other guardians of a minor discover that the minor has committed不良 conduct, they shall promptly stop it and strengthen discipline.

Article 30 Where a public security organ, a residents' committee, or a villagers' committee discovers that a minor within its jurisdiction has committed不良 conduct, it shall promptly stop it and urge the parents or other guardians of the minor to perform their guardianship duties according to law.

Article 32 Schools and families shall strengthen communication and establish a home-school cooperation mechanism. Where a school decides to take management and education measures against a minor student, it shall promptly inform the parents or other guardians of the student; the parents or other guardians of the minor student shall support and cooperate with the school in carrying out management and education.

Article 33 Where a minor student steals a small amount of property, or commits student bullying acts such as beating, insulting, intimidating, or forcibly demanding property, and the circumstances are minor, the school may take corresponding management and education measures in accordance with the provisions of Article 31 of this Law.

Article 34 Where a minor student skips classes or plays truant, the school shall promptly contact the parents or other guardians of the student to ascertain the relevant situation; if there is no justifiable reason, the school and the parents or other guardians of the minor student shall urge the student to return to school for study.

Article 35 Where a minor stays out all night without justifiable reason or runs away from home, the parents or other guardians and the boarding school where the minor studies shall promptly search for the minor, and if necessary, report to the public security organ.
Any person who shelters a minor who stays out all night or runs away from home shall promptly contact the parents or other guardians or the school where the minor studies; if contact cannot be made, the person shall promptly report to the public security organ.

Article 36 Where a minor is found or reported to be staying out all night, running away from home, or wandering on the streets, the public security organs, public place management institutions, and other entities shall promptly take effective protective measures, notify the parents or other guardians and the boarding school where the minor studies, and if necessary, escort the minor back to his or her residence or school; if contact cannot be made with the parents or other guardians or the school, the minor shall be escorted to a relief and protection institution to receive assistance.

Article 37 Where the parents or other guardians of a minor or a school discovers that the minor organizes or participates in a gang that commits不良 conduct, they shall promptly stop it; where it is discovered that the gang is suspected of committing illegal or criminal acts, they shall immediately report to the public security organ.

Article 39 Where the parents or other guardians of a minor, a school, a residents' committee, or a villagers' committee discovers that any person instigates, coerces, or entices a minor to commit serious不良 conduct, they shall immediately report to the public security organ. Upon receiving a report or discovering the aforesaid circumstances, the public security organ shall promptly investigate and handle the matter according to law; with respect to a minor whose personal safety is threatened, effective protective measures shall be taken immediately.

Article 40 Where a public security organ receives a report or discovers that a minor has committed serious不良 conduct, it shall promptly stop the conduct, investigate and handle the matter according to law, and may order the parents or other guardians of the minor to eliminate or mitigate the illegal consequences and take measures to strictly discipline the minor.

Article 42 When carrying out correctional education for a minor, the public security organ may, as needed, invite schools, residents' committees, villagers' committees, and social organizations such as social work service institutions to participate.
The parents or other guardians of the minor shall actively cooperate with the implementation of correctional education measures and shall not obstruct, hinder, or neglect them.

Article 43 Where the parents or other guardians of a minor with serious不良 conduct or the school where the minor studies is unable to discipline the minor or discipline proves ineffective, they may apply to the education administrative department; after evaluation and approval by the specialized education steering committee, the education administrative department shall decide to send the minor to a specialized school for specialized education.

Article 45 Where a minor commits an act provided for in the Criminal Law and criminal punishment is not imposed due to the minor not having reached the statutory age of criminal responsibility, upon evaluation and approval by the specialized education steering committee, the education administrative department together with the public security organ may decide to carry out specialized correctional education for the minor.
The people's government of a province, autonomous region, or municipality directly under the Central Government shall, based on local actual conditions, designate at least one specialized school to set up specialized venues by way of separate campuses or classes, etc., to carry out specialized correctional education for the minors specified in the preceding paragraph.
The specialized venues specified in the preceding paragraph shall implement closed-loop management. The public security organs and judicial administrative departments shall be responsible for the correctional work of the minors, and the education administrative departments shall undertake the education work of the minors.

Article 46 A specialized school shall, at an appropriate time in each semester, request the specialized education steering committee to evaluate the situation of the minor students receiving specialized education. Where, upon evaluation, a student is deemed suitable to be transferred back to a regular school for study, the specialized education steering committee shall make a written recommendation to the original decision-making organ, and the original decision-making organ shall decide whether to transfer the minor student back to a regular school for study.
Where the original decision-making organ decides to transfer a minor student back to a regular school, the original school from which the student came shall not refuse to accept the student; if, due to special circumstances, it is inappropriate to transfer the student back to the original school, the education administrative department shall arrange for the student to transfer to another school.

Article 47 A specialized school shall educate and correct minors receiving specialized education by different grades and categories, carry out targeted moral education, rule-of-law education, and mental health education, and, based on actual circumstances, provide vocational education; for minors who have not completed compulsory education, the school shall ensure that they continue to receive compulsory education.
The student status of minor students in specialized schools shall be retained in their original schools, and if they meet the graduation requirements, the original schools shall issue graduation certificates.

Article 48 A specialized school shall strengthen contact with the parents or other guardians of minors receiving specialized education, regularly provide feedback to them on the correction and education of the minors, and facilitate visits by the parents or other guardians, relatives, and others to see the minors.

Article 49 Where a minor or his or her parents or other guardians are dissatisfied with an administrative decision provided for in this Chapter, they may apply for administrative reconsideration or institute administrative proceedings according to law.

Article 50 When handling criminal cases involving minors, the public security organs, the People's Procuratorates, and the People's Courts shall, based on the physiological and psychological characteristics of the minors and the circumstances of the crimes, carry out targeted rule-of-law education.
Where, in educating minors involved in criminal cases, the participation of adult relatives other than their legal representatives, or teachers, counselors, or other persons is conducive to influencing and saving the minors, the public security organs, the People's Procuratorates, and the People's Courts shall invite such persons to participate in relevant activities.

Fifty-one Public security organs, People's Procuratorates, and People's Courts, when handling criminal cases involving minors, may conduct social investigations on their own or entrust relevant social organizations or institutions to investigate the growth experience, causes of crime, guardianship, education, and other matters of the juvenile criminal suspect or defendant; based on actual needs and with the consent of the juvenile criminal suspect or defendant and their legal representatives, they may conduct psychological assessments of the juvenile criminal suspect or defendant.
The reports of social investigations and psychological assessments may serve as reference for handling cases and educating minors.

Fifty-two Public security organs, People's Procuratorates, and People's Courts shall, when granting release on bail pending investigation or trial to a minor who has no fixed domicile and cannot provide a guarantor, designate a suitable adult as a guarantor; when necessary, they may arrange for the minor released on bail pending investigation or trial to receive social observation.

Fifty-three Minors who are detained, arrested, or serving sentences in juvenile correctional facilities shall be held, managed, and educated separately from adults. Community correction for minors shall be carried out separately from adults.
For minors in the above situations who have not completed compulsory education, public security organs, People's Procuratorates, People's Courts, and judicial administrative departments shall cooperate with education administrative departments to ensure that they continue to receive compulsory education.

Fifty-four Juvenile correctional facilities and community correction institutions shall strengthen legal education for juvenile offenders and juvenile community correction recipients, and shall provide vocational education to them based on actual circumstances.

Fifty-five Community correction institutions shall inform juvenile community correction recipients of the relevant provisions on resettlement and assistance, and shall cooperate with resettlement and assistance work departments to implement or resolve issues such as schooling and employment of juvenile community correction recipients.

Fifty-six For minors who have been released upon completion of a sentence, the juvenile correctional facility shall notify their parents or other guardians in advance to pick them up on time, and shall assist in implementing resettlement and assistance measures. If there are no parents or other guardians, or if the parents or other guardians cannot be identified, the juvenile correctional facility shall in advance notify the judicial administrative department of the minor's original registered residence or place of residence to arrange for personnel to pick them up on time, and the civil affairs department or the residents' committee or villagers' committee shall act as guardian for the minor according to law.

Fifty-seven The parents or other guardians of minors, as well as schools, residents' committees, and villagers' committees, shall take effective assistance and education measures for minors undergoing community correction or released upon completion of a sentence, and shall assist judicial organs and relevant departments in properly carrying out resettlement and assistance work.
Residents' committees and villagers' committees may engage retired personnel, volunteers, or other persons of excellent ideological and moral character, upright style, and enthusiastic about work concerning minors to assist in the resettlement and assistance work as mentioned in the preceding paragraph.

Fifty-eight Minors released upon completion of a sentence or undergoing community correction shall enjoy the same rights as other minors according to law in terms of resuming schooling, entering a higher school, employment, etc., and no unit or individual shall discriminate against them.

Fifty-nine If a minor's criminal record is sealed according to law, public security organs, People's Procuratorates, People's Courts, and judicial administrative departments shall not provide it to any unit or individual, except when judicial organs need it for case handling or relevant units inquire in accordance with relevant state regulations. Units and individuals that inquire according to law shall keep the relevant record information confidential.
The records of minors receiving specialized correctional education or specialized education, as well as records of administrative penalties, compulsory criminal measures, and non-prosecution, shall be governed by the provisions of the preceding paragraph.
Sixty The People's Procuratorates shall supervise the prevention of reoffending by minors through the exercise of procuratorial power according to law.

Sixty-one Public security organs, People's Procuratorates, and People's Courts, when discovering that parents or other guardians of minors who have engaged in serious misbehavior fail to perform their guardianship duties according to law, shall reprimand them and may order them to accept family education guidance.

Sixty-two If a school or its faculty and staff violate the provisions of this Law by failing to perform duties in preventing juvenile delinquency, or by abusing or discriminating against relevant minors, the education administration and other departments shall order correction and circulate a notice of criticism; if the circumstances are serious, the directly responsible supervisors and other directly responsible personnel shall be given sanctions according to law. If it constitutes a violation of public security administration, the public security organ shall impose a public security administration penalty according to law.
If faculty or staff instigate, coerce, or induce minors to engage in misbehavior or serious misbehavior, or if they are of bad character and have a vile influence, the education administrative department or the school shall dismiss or discharge them according to law.

Sixty-three If, in violation of the provisions of this Law, relevant minors are discriminated against in terms of resuming schooling, entering a higher school, employment, etc., the unit or the education, human resources and social security departments shall order correction; if correction is refused, the directly responsible supervisors or other directly responsible personnel shall be given sanctions according to law.

Sixty-four If relevant social organizations or institutions and their staff abuse or discriminate against minors receiving social observation, or issue false social investigation or psychological assessment reports, the civil affairs and judicial administrative departments shall impose sanctions on the directly responsible supervisors or other directly responsible personnel according to law; if it constitutes a violation of public security administration, the public security organ shall impose a public security administration penalty.

Sixty-five If a person instigates, coerces, or induces a minor to engage in misbehavior or serious misbehavior, and it constitutes a violation of public security administration, the public security organ shall impose a public security administration penalty according to law.

Sixty-six If state organs and their staff abuse power, neglect duties, or engage in malpractice for personal gain in the work of preventing juvenile delinquency, the directly responsible supervisors and other directly responsible personnel shall be given sanctions according to law.
Sixty-seven If a violation of the provisions of this Law constitutes a crime, criminal liability shall be investigated according to law.
Sixty-eight This Law shall come into force as of June 1, 2021.
